title: Stable handoff playbook for variant misassignments and cross-region reroute mitigation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: A production capacity event on 2026-02-12 exposed a sequence of smart-routing failures where requests were routed to incompatible model variants across regions, causing persistent reroute loops and elevated tail latency for affected customers. This ticket captures the post-incident action plan, owner assignments, and implementation notes for preventing recurrence.

Impact: Several high-throughput customers experienced 3-12x token latency and a 15% increase in 5xxs during the incident window. Impact surface included hosted API and Dedicated pools in eu-west and us-east, with cascading retries amplifying capacity pressure.

Root cause analysis: The immediate cause was a policy deployment that introduced a precedence inversion: a new regional override rule lacked a compatibility predicate and returned a different model "flavor" (quantized vs full-precision) without verifying runtime compatibility. The routing state machine then performed sticky handoffs based on the changed policy snapshot while downstream capacity signal lagged, producing oscillating fanout and cross-region reroutes. Contributing factors: 1) policy schemas lacked an explicit variant-compatibility checksum, 2) no admission guard for sudden policy precedence flips, 3) limited telemetry linking routing-decision IDs to model-version hashes, 4) retry/backoff heuristics amplified traffic to fallback variants.

Mitigation summary already applied: 1) Immediate rollback of the policy change and temporary tightening of retry windows. 2) Short-term throttle on cross-region fanout from the affected router shard. 3) Emergency hotfix to disable variant-sticky handoff for canary policies.

Goals for this ticket:
- Implement a validation and admission flow that prevents policy changes introducing incompatible variant mappings without explicit opt-in.
- Add a lightweight checksum/hash to model variant descriptors and require handoff integrity checks at admission and at router decision time.
- Introduce a circuit-breaker that detects rapid cross-region reroute loops (more than N cycles within T seconds) and forces a safe fallback (local capacity-only) while alerting SRE.
- Enrich routing telemetry so a single request ID surfaces: requested model, resolved variant hash, policy snapshot id, and routing transitions.
- Create a canary policy rollout process with staged precedence increases and automatic rollback on SLO regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Policy API rejects precedence changes that would map a route to an incompatible variant unless override flag set and signed.
- Router rejects handoff if variant checksum differs from policy snapshot and logs a coherent error that surfaces in dashboards.
- New circuit-breaker prevented a synthetic reroute loop in the canary test harness and has covered unit/integration tests.
- Dashboards show routing decision traces for 100% of sampled requests for 7 days after rollout.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Strict admission checks add operational friction for rapid policy fixes; we add an explicit opt-in override for emergency fixes that requires two approvers and audit logging.
- Circuit-breaker behavior is conservative to avoid false positives; we will iterate thresholds after canary feedback.

Full incident writeup and timeline are linked in links below.
